What We Do

Full-Service Pediatric Practice Revenue Cycle Management

Pediatric billing combines well-child preventive visit coding, vaccine product and administration billing, developmental and behavioral screening codes, and sick visit E/M. PMEX manages every revenue stream so pediatric practices capture payment on every preventive and acute care encounter.

Well-Child Visit Coding

Preventive medicine visits (99381 to 99395) coded by age group and new vs. established status.

Vaccine Administration Billing

Immunization administration codes (90460, 90461, 90471, 90472) billed per vaccine.

Vaccine Product Billing

Vaccine product codes (90633 to 90756) billed separately from administration.

Developmental Screening

M-CHAT (96110) and other developmental screening codes billed per screen administered.

Sick Visit E/M Coding

Same-day sick visit billed with modifier 25 alongside the preventive visit when separately documented.

ADHD Management Billing

ADHD E/M visits coded at correct complexity with behavioral health coordination where applicable.

Sound Familiar?

Common Pediatrics Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Well-child visit and same-day sick visit not both billed, losing the sick visit revenue.

PMEX submits the sick visit E/M with modifier 25 on every encounter where a separate problem is documented alongside the preventive visit.

Vaccine administration codes billed without counseling component (90460/90461) for patients under age 6.

PMEX applies 90460 for the first vaccine and 90461 for each additional vaccine when physician counseling is documented for patients under 6.

Vaccine product codes not submitted alongside the administration codes.

PMEX submits the vaccine product CPT code separately from the administration code on every immunization encounter.

Developmental screening (96110) not billed when M-CHAT or similar tool is administered.

PMEX identifies developmental screening from the well-child visit documentation and submits 96110 on every visit where a standardized screening tool is documented.

Age group applied incorrectly on preventive visit code, misclassifying the visit level.

PMEX confirms the patient age on the date of service and applies the correct preventive medicine CPT code for the age group.

ADHD follow-up visits coded at low complexity when the MDM supports a higher level.

PMEX codes ADHD management visits from 2021 MDM criteria, capturing the full complexity of multi-problem behavioral and medical management.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Pediatrics Billing

Pediatric practices lose 14 to 22 percent of revenue to preventive visit miscoding, vaccine billing omissions, and same-day sick visit bundling errors.

PATTERN 01

Same-Day Sick Visit Not Billed Alongside Well-Child Visit

Child presents for 4-year well-child visit. Parent also reports ear pain. Physician examines the ear and diagnoses otitis media. Only the preventive visit (99394) submitted. Sick visit E/M (99213) with modifier 25 not billed. $85 per encounter in sick visit revenue lost when a separate problem is managed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies same-day well-child plus acute problem encounters from the visit documentation and submits the sick visit E/M with modifier 25 alongside the preventive visit, confirmed against documentation that a separately identifiable problem-focused service was provided.

PATTERN 02

Vaccine Counseling Component Not Billed for Under-6 Patients

3-year-old receives DTaP, IPV, and MMR vaccines. Physician provides counseling for each vaccine. 90471 and 90472 submitted for administration. 90460 and 90461 not used. Lost revenue: $15 per counseling component. Three vaccines with counseling: $45 per immunization visit for patients under 6.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies 90460 for the first vaccine with physician counseling and 90461 for each additional vaccine with counseling on every immunization visit for patients under age 6 where physician counseling is documented.

PATTERN 03

Developmental Screening Not Separately Billed

M-CHAT administered at 18-month well-child visit. Screening documented in the chart. 96110 not submitted. $28 per screening visit in developmental screening revenue not captured. Applies to every visit where a standardized screening tool is used and not billed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews well-child visit documentation for standardized developmental screening tool administration and submits 96110 on every visit where a screen such as M-CHAT, ASQ, or MCHAT-R is documented as having been administered.
